correctness.rationale: The conserved quadratic energy and full stage span are proved by direct linear-algebra identities. The prescribed correction is a convex scalar quadratic; its completed square gives an if-and-only-if real-root criterion. Maximization on the whole phase interval and invertibility of the midpoint map prove the sharp all-phase step threshold. A scaled-rotation conjugacy transports uniform energy angle to uniform predictor angle, and exact integration of the arcsine density gives the closed form and the two asymptotics. The rational counterexample and 6,563 tests in verify.py corroborate critical computations. Finite checks are not relied on as infinite or exhaustive proof.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly determines whether a convex-invariant numerical correction equation is solvable for all initial phases and gives the prevalence of failed root solves when it is not. Its critical square-root law and inverse-square rare-success tail measure practical breakdown and the effect of anisotropy (uniform threshold decays as kappa^{-3/2}). Unlike arbitrary toy data, this is the canonical anisotropic quadratic oscillator for invariant-preserving RK projection. No unproved extension to other methods or multiple time steps is claimed.
